summary: The symbolist poet Renee Vivien was, in Sarah Parker's words, 'one of Barney's former lovers' by the time Olive Custance came to Paris around 1901 and befriended her. Barney's own memoir Souvenirs Indiscrets (1960) records, as Parker reports it, that Barney tried to persuade Custance to join her and Vivien in recreating a Sapphic community at Mytilene, and that the plan foundered on Vivien's jealousy - which is the one moment where this pair's history bears directly on the Wilde circle, since Custance married Lord Alfred Douglas the following year. Custance kept up contact with both women after returning to London in 1901.

sources.quote: Lorsque nous foulâmes cette poussière consacrée par les sandales de Sapho et de ses poétesses, nous reprîmes conscience de notre pèlerinage, malgré les irruptions modernes. … Les nuits étaient plus belles que toutes celles que nous avions connues et, dès la première, quel cri de victoire je dus étouffer !
sources.context: Barney's own account of the Mytilene journey she made with Renée Vivien - they travelled from Vienna on the Orient-Express via Constantinople. The elision drops a paragraph on the modern island's disappointments (Barney notes they saw not one woman worthy of Sappho's descent, only dockers, fishermen and shepherds). Translation of the second sentence: 'The nights were more beautiful than any we had known, and from the very first, what a cry of victory I had to stifle!' Barney's is the only first-hand account of this journey; Vivien's side survives as the poems Barney quotes around it.
sources.supports: The participant's own account of the Mytilene journey and of the nights there - the closest thing to a direct statement of the physical relationship that either woman left, and in Barney's own voice.

sources.quote: Dans l'enchantement de ce séjour, sans courrier et sans autre souvenir, nous louâmes deux petites villas réunies par le même verger, car Renée était résolue à ne plus quitter Mytilène, où elle m'attendrait « fidèlement et sans bouger » si, plus tard, j'avais affaire ailleurs. … « Pourquoi ne formerions-nous pas ici même cette école de poésie tant rêvée, où celles qui vibrent de poésie, de jeunesse et d'amour, viendraient à nous, telles ces poétesses de jadis arrivant de toutes parts pour entourer Sapho ? » Renée était en effet séduite par cette perspective.
sources.context: The Mytilene plan itself, in the participant's words: two villas joined by one orchard, Vivien resolved never to leave the island, and Barney proposing the school of poetry there. The elision drops Barney's exchange with Vivien about having 'business elsewhere', which is what prompts the proposal. The guillemets are Barney's.
sources.supports: The Mytilene community plan, first-hand - a shared household and a Sapphic poetry school proposed by one participant and welcomed by the other.

sources.quote: [Renée] readily traded seats with Eva and every night thereafter sat holding hands with Natalie, both of them transported by Wagner's music. … she promised to meet Natalie in Vienna and to go with her to Lesbos. … their poems sang of this enchanted island with its balmy seas, fragrance of jasmine and beautiful nights full of love. They rented two little villas in an orchard, where Renée vowed she would stay, forever waiting for Natalie.
sources.context: Wickes on the Bayreuth reconciliation and the voyage to Mytilene. Barney marked the reunion by giving Vivien the prose-poem sequence Je me souviens, 'commemorating their love and expressing her sense of loss'.
sources.supports: Biographer account of the Barney-Vivien relationship.
